qualitative.gate_2_reason: Non-essential private-label store credit cards and promotional financing with high APRs, late fee dependency, and regulatory/CFPB risk.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 2 (Rejected – G2 Essential Need). Synchrony Financial operates private-label store credit card programs and point-of-sale promotional financing for retail partners and elective healthcare (CareCredit). Store credit cards are an easily forgone, non-essential financing tool for discretionary consumer purchases, carrying high APRs (often 30%+), deferred-interest penalties, and vulnerability to CFPB late fee caps and consumer credit degradation.
qualitative.evidence: Synchrony's loan portfolio is concentrated in private-label credit cards with major retailers (Amazon, Lowe's) and CareCredit. The business model depends on high APRs (averaging ~21-23%+ net interest margin), late fees, and promotional deferred interest, exposing it to severe regulatory scrutiny (CFPB $8 late fee rule) and cyclical credit loss shocks (FY24 net charge-off rate spiked to 6.31%). Retail partners hold strong bargaining power through Retailer Share Arrangements (RSAs) and can switch providers (as Walmart and Gap did).
